tagline.text: An April festival of sharing where ten Mountain Province towns gather in Bontoc

location.label: Location
location.text: Bontoc, Mountain Province (street events on Bontoc's main street, performances at Eyeb grounds and hall)

best_season.label: Best time to visit

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱3,000~8,000 (2 nights and 3 days from Manila, covering transport, lodging and meals)

children.text: The Lang-ay Festival is a founding anniversary celebration held in Bontoc, Mountain Province, every first week of April, with traditional dances and songs from ten municipalities, a street feast and an agro-trade fair. In 2026, however, the main events were canceled because of the national energy emergency, so check first whether it is being held.

The Lang-ay Festival is the flagship April festival of Mountain Province in the Cordillera region of northern Philippines. "Lang-ay" is understood in the local language to mean communities sharing with one another, and the provincial capital, Bontoc, is the center of the events. It runs for about a week around April 7, the province's founding anniversary, and the first edition is said to have been held in 2005. One thing to know first: in March 2026 the provincial government canceled the main events of the 2026 Lang-ay Festival under the national energy emergency (Executive Order No. 110), and said it would mark the province's 59th founding anniversary on April 7 with only modest commemorative activities. The news changed quickly during March, from "scaled down" to "fully canceled," so before you go, be sure to check the official announcements of the Mountain Province government and the festival committee's Facebook page.

Knowing the history makes the festival easier to appreciate. Mountain Province was known as Gran Cordillera in the Spanish period and was established as a province in 1908 under American rule. In 1966 it was split into Benguet, Ifugao and Kalinga-Apayao, and Kalinga and Apayao separated again in 1995. April 7 was set as the founding anniversary by a provincial board resolution in 1980 and made official by a proclamation in 1993. Lang-ay was started to celebrate that anniversary by the governor of the time in 2005, has been run with a private committee since 2015, and was not held from 2020 to 2022 because of COVID-19. The 2024, 2025 and 2026 festivals are described as the 17th, 18th and 19th editions.

Ten municipalities take part: Tadian, Besao, Bauko, Sagada, Sabangan, Bontoc, Sadanga, Barlig, Natonin and Paracelis. Each has its own festival, such as the "Begnas" thanksgiving for a good harvest, and Lang-ay is presented as the event that brings them all together. That lets you compare each town's traditional costumes, dances, songs and performances in one place.

The most popular part is "Lang-ay on the Street," held on Bontoc's closed-off main street. It is a street feast where people share local traditional food and tapuey rice wine, and visitors are asked to take only as much as they can eat. The highlights that follow are the street dancing parade of the towns and the cultural performances at the Eyeb grounds and hall.

Bontoc's main street is closed to vehicles and lined with stalls for a street feast that shares traditional food. You can taste local dishes and rice wine. Check the announcements each year for the time and place. Bontoc is a small town, so the street is easy to take in at a glance and you can walk between the venues and your lodging.

blocks.title: Street dancing parade of ten towns

children.text: Young people and elders from ten towns, including Tadian, Sagada and Bauko, perform traditional dances and songs in a parade. The choreography is described as keeping to traditional movements. Costumes, ornaments and instruments differ slightly from town to town, so it is fun to compare them.
After the parade, cultural performances and contests are known to be held at the Eyeb grounds and hall in Bontoc. The 2025 fireworks were also held at the Eyeb grounds.
On opening day in 2024, elders performed "Tukab di Gusi," opening a jar of rice wine and asking for blessings. Check whether the same ritual is held every year.

An agricultural and specialty-products trade fair opens along with the festival, where you can browse local goods. In 2026, because many vendors had already paid their fees, there was even discussion of keeping only the trade fair, so check whether it is held each year.

According to festival materials, the program has at times included a night of gong music and dance, traditional games, a traditional cooking event, a food event featuring "patupat" (a snack of glutinous rice and sugarcane juice), and the search for Miss Mountain Province. Details differ each year, so check the announcements.

Mountain Province designated April 7 as its founding anniversary. A parade and commemorative events are held, and the festival often wraps up around this day. In 2026, it was announced that only this anniversary would be observed, in a modest way.

blocks.title: Pairing with the rest of the Cordillera

children.text: Adding the caves of Sagada, the Banaue Rice Terraces and Batad before or after the event makes for a fuller trip. Early April is the tail end of the dry season, so the weather is also relatively good.

5–6 hours

Arrive in Bontoc, drop your bags at your lodging and walk to the main street.
Browse the agro-trade fair and the stalls to see local products and food.
Around sunset, walk through Bontoc town to see the market and village scenery.
Have dinner near your lodging and turn in early.
Head to the main street early on the second morning and find a spot for the street dancing parade.
Watch the parade of the ten towns and the performances at the Eyeb grounds.
Check the last bus toward Baguio and head out.
The exact dates and order of events change from year to year, so the times above are only an example for planning a day's route.

Sagada is a separate registered destination, so see its entry for a detailed itinerary.

From the Slaughterhouse terminal in Baguio, buses such as GL Trans and Lizardo go toward Bontoc and Sagada. One guide gives about

The Banaue–Bontoc leg is given with different travel times in different guides, so confirm locally.
You can get around the center of Bontoc on foot.
To nearby towns you take jeepneys and tricycles; confirm fares and schedules locally.
A private car or rental car is not recommended for inexperienced drivers because the mountain roads are narrow and winding. A car with a driver is safer.
During the festival, the main street may be closed to traffic, so the location of jeepney stops may change.

The Lang-ay Festival is held around the first week of April. The year's schedule is confirmed only by announcements from the Mountain Province government, so check first whether it is being held before you buy a flight or bus ticket.
The Cordillera is high, so mornings and evenings are cool even in April while the sun is strong during the day. Bring a light jacket and sunscreen.

Even if you miss the festival, the Cordillera is a good place to travel in the November–May dry season. Early April is the tail end of the dry season, so rain is less of a worry, but confirm whether the festival is held and its schedule before booking lodging.

Bontoc is a small town with few places to stay, and they fill up early during the festival. Book about a month ahead if you can, and if nothing is available, you can stay in Sagada or Banaue and come in for the day.

Typical foods are traditional rice dishes, pork and chicken dishes, and tapuey rice wine. At the street feast you can taste the traditional food that is handed out, so bringing a plate and a water bottle is handy.

Bontoc is a day's travel from Baguio, so starting from Manila usually means spending one day on the road. A simple plan is to rest in Baguio or Bontoc on the first day and watch the events on the second. Besides what is handed out at the street feast, you can easily find rice and meat dishes at local eateries, but they get crowded during the festival, so go early.
Before you go, check the Mountain Province government and the official Lang-ay Festival Facebook page for this year's schedule and whether it is being held.
Lodging and buses are crowded in early April, so secure your tickets and room in advance.
At the street feast, it is local etiquette to take only as much as you will eat.
Claim your spot early so you can see the parade well.
The sun is strong during the day and mornings and evenings are cool, so dress in layers.
Ask permission before photographing performers and elders.
Carry cash in small bills. There are few ATMs in the mountains.
The mountain road from Baguio to Bontoc is long, so motion-sickness medicine can help.
In years when the festival is canceled, check the announcements for whether anything is held for the April 7 founding anniversary.
Room rates can rise and rooms run short during the festival, so check the cancellation policy of your booking.
The main events of the 2026 Lang-ay Festival were canceled because of the national energy emergency. Check each year whether it is being held first.
The festival schedule and program change every year and may be canceled. Make nonrefundable bookings only after it is confirmed.
Mountain roads can see landslides or closures in rain, so leave slack in your schedule.
Photography may be restricted at rituals and traditional events, so follow the instructions.
Do not drink too much at drinking events. Tapuey can be strong.
The last buses tend to leave early, so confirm your return time.
Bontoc is a small town with few ATMs and money changers. Bring plenty of cash in advance.
A cave and valley town close to Bontoc that pairs well with the festival. Confirm transport and travel time locally.
UNESCO World Heritage rice terraces in the southern Cordillera, easy to add before or after the festival.
